approachQuestion.prompt:
Copy a cross-linked inspection chain

Input: head of a finite singly linked chain of n distinct node objects. Each node has an integer label, next pointing to the next chain node or null, and cross pointing to any node in this same chain or null. Next links form a simple chain; cross links may form cycles or self-links. Return the head of a deep copy: preserve all labels and next/cross relationships, but every copied node is new and no copied pointer targets an original node. Original nodes are immutable, including temporarily.

Example 1: chain labels = [5,5,9], cross target indices = [2,0,2] using zero-based next-order indices. Output: three new nodes with labels [5,5,9] and cross target indices [2,0,2], with the last cross pointing to that copied last node. Example 2: head = null. Output: null. 0 ≤ n ≤ 200,000. Object identity, not label equality, identifies nodes. Identity hashing has expected amortized constant cost.

Constraints: input is immutable; all identifiers and numeric entries are signed 32-bit integers unless specified. Arithmetic uses signed 64-bit integers. Prefer the least expected running-time growth, then avoid unnecessary asymptotic auxiliary storage. Non-adversarial hashing of fixed-size integer keys/tuples has expected amortized constant cost.

options.text: Traverse next links, allocating one copied node per original and mapping original object identity to its copy. Traverse again and assign copied next/cross using map lookups for original targets.
options.feedback: Every original target already has its own copy before wiring begins, including forward references, self-links and cycles; identity keys distinguish duplicate labels.

options.text: Copy the next chain first. For each cross link, scan original and copied chains in parallel to find that original target and assign the corresponding copied node.
options.feedback: This is correct because every target belongs to the chain, but repeatedly searching for the same identity adds removable work compared with direct lookup.

options.text: Map each integer label to one copied node and wire all references by target labels.
options.feedback: In the example, the two original nodes labeled 5 are distinct and have different reference identities. One label-keyed copy merges them.

options.text: Allocate new nodes for the next chain but copy cross pointers unchanged from each original node.
options.feedback: A non-null copied cross pointer would still target an original node, violating the deep-copy requirement.

feedback.reason: Use an original-object to copied-object relation to preserve arbitrary reference topology when labels are not unique.
details: In a first iterative next-chain traversal, allocate one new output node per original node and store original-identity→copy in a map. In a second traversal, set each copy’s next and cross to null or the map entry for the original target. Return the mapped head. Do not mutate originals or recurse.
Allocate all copies before wiring links, so forward references and self-links already have destinations. Key by object identity: equal labels do not mean the same original node.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method “Copy a cross-linked inspection chain — analyzed method”, n is the number of nodes on the next chain. Allocating/copying one node and identity-key hashing each take constant/expected amortized constant time; copied nodes are the returned output. Choose its time and auxiliary-space pair. Use the tightest standard bound for the worst legal input for the stated size parameters, with expected time over non-adversarial hashing. Fixed-width integer and fixed-size tuple hash operations take expected amortized O(1); arithmetic, comparison and copying one integer take O(1). Auxiliary space excludes the supplied input and returned result, includes all maps, sets, temporary copies and call stacks. The method is iterative, with constant call-stack space.

feedback.reason: Two chain passes use an original-to-copy map; returned copied nodes are excluded.
details: Use an original-object to copied-object relation to preserve arbitrary reference topology when labels are not unique.

Two next-chain passes each visit n nodes. Constant-size allocation and expected amortized identity-map operations per node give expected O(n+1). Cross links are looked up rather than traversed recursively.
All n newly allocated copied nodes belong to the returned structure and are excluded. The separate identity map has n entries and is auxiliary, giving O(n+1); the iterative call stack is constant.
“Expected O(n + 1) time; O(n + 1) auxiliary space.”: Correct under the stated expected/amortized hashing model.
“Expected O(n + 1) time; O(1) auxiliary space because copied nodes are output.”: Copied nodes are excluded, but the separate original-to-copy map still retains n entries.
“Expected O(n² + 1) time; O(n + 1) auxiliary space.”: The map avoids repeated chain searches; two traversals visit each node a constant number of times.
“Expected O(n + 1) time; O(h + 1) auxiliary space for a recursive depth h.”: The stated method is iterative, not recursive; its map requires n entries regardless of cross-link depth.
